ds: Operation of unlicensed betting, underground casinos and online gambling, and manipulation of sporting events for betting profit. Money is laundered through bets, payment processors and agents, with corruption of athletes or officials.

cn.rt: Customers fund offshore or unlicensed betting via card and bank payments, and use accounts as pass-through wallets; mostly digital.

rat: Betting payments via card/bank to disguised merchants, nested processors, e-wallets and crypto.

ind.n: Payments to unlicensed gambling operators or via nested processors
ind.cx: Card or bank payments to merchants disguised under other categories.
ind.ds: Payments go to operators, platforms or merchants that are absent from regulatory registers, imitate a legitimate firm, or process under a disguised merchant category.
ind.cn: Unlicensed or cloned operator receiving payments

ind.n: Many accounts funding a few betting accounts or agents
ind.cx: Pooling of funds to bookmakers or agents.
ind.ds: Numerous unrelated payers send frequent, often small, payments to one account, wallet or beneficiary, or one funder pays many beneficiaries, with no clear commercial relationship.
ind.cn: Many unrelated senders paying a single account or recipient

ind.n: Bets with minimal risk, such as opposing outcomes at different books
ind.cx: Low-risk betting and quick withdrawals to launder.
ind.ds: Low-risk betting and quick withdrawals to launder.

ind.n: Unusual betting patterns on lower-league or youth matches
ind.cx: Large late stakes on obscure markets.
ind.ds: Large late stakes on obscure markets.

ind.n: Players or officials receive payments from betting-linked parties
ind.cx: Payments to athletes, referees from unrelated parties.
ind.ds: Payments to athletes, referees from unrelated parties.

ind.n: Deposits and withdrawals with little betting activity
ind.cx: Account used as e-wallet with minimal play.
ind.fp: Players may deposit and cash out.
ind.ds: Substantial funds are deposited or bought in with minimal gambling or betting activity before withdrawal.
ind.cn: Large buy-in or deposits with little underlying activity

ind.n: Underground casino or card house with cash and chip sales
ind.cx: Cash-heavy venue with transfers by chat apps.
ind.ds: Cash-heavy venue with transfers by chat apps.

ind.n: Use of crypto and prepaid cards for gambling top-ups
ind.cx: Layering via crypto into betting accounts.
ind.fp: Crypto betting is legal in places.
ind.ds: Layering via crypto into betting accounts.

ind.n: Gambling operator with threshold-avoiding ownership, white-label dependence or frequent brand and URL changes
ind.cx: Illegal or grey-market operators hide ownership, rely on white-label providers and rotate URLs and brands.
ind.fp: Legitimate multi-brand operators with disclosed group structures and licences.
ind.ds: An operator or platform customer structures shareholdings to stay under regulatory-check thresholds, relies on loosely overseen white-label or third-party providers, or frequently changes its website, brand or company name.

ind.n: Gambling payments disguised as ordinary retail purchases through sham merchants
ind.cx: Illicit operators process gambling deposits through sham domestic merchant identities.
ind.fp: Genuine retailers with mis-coded merchant category codes.
ind.ds: Card or account payments to what appears to be a domestic retailer are in fact deposits to an illicit gambling operator using a borrowed or fake merchant identity.

ind.n: High volume of small payments through phone-number payment aliases, quickly forwarded
ind.cx: Unlawful gambling proceeds micro-laundered through many small payments to mule payment aliases.
ind.fp: Small sellers, sporting clubs or shared-expense groups collecting many small payments.
ind.ds: An account receives many low-value inbound payments addressed to a phone-number payment alias (e.g. PayID) and moves the funds on in a tiered pattern, consistent with micro-laundering of unlawful gambling proceeds.

ctl.ds: Monitors merchant-level patterns such as ticket size, refund, void and chargeback rates, descriptor mismatch and cross-merchant flows. It identifies transaction laundering, bust-out and illicit merchants.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

ctl.n: Agent and distribution network due diligence
ctl.ds: Vets, trains, caps and monitors agents, sub-agents and distributors who onboard customers or move funds on the institution's behalf, including quality visits, outlier analysis and disclosure of principals. It limits control failures at the edge of a distribution network.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

Surveils chip transfers, buy-in versus play, low-risk or hedged betting, unusual stakes and collusive play between accounts or players. It detects use of gaming or betting products to launder or manipulate outcomes.
Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.

Restricts cash-out and cheque issue to evidenced winnings, prohibits redemption to third parties and issues win certificates only on verified records, with periodic audit. It prevents gaming proceeds being used as a conduit for illicit funds.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.
Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

ctl.n: Gatekeeper and company service provider due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses licensing, CDD standards and client mix of formation agents, lawyers and similar professionals and monitors formation volumes and concentration. It targets professional enablers.

Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.

Verifies merchant identity, business model, website content and expected volumes before activation and re-verifies on change, with remediation of weak merchants. It stops fronts and disguised businesses entering payment channels.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.
